title: How Costco Makes Money Selling a $1.50 Hot Dog
description:
How does Costco make money selling a hot dog for $1.50? The price hasn't moved since the 1980s, even though inflation says it should cost about $4.40. Here's the story behind it: the co-founder who said "If you raise the effing hot dog, I will kill you. Figure it out.", the $4.99 chicken and its $300 million plant, and the real business underneath it all: the membership card.

Chapters
0:00 A $1.50 hot dog
0:49 Where the idea came from
1:15 The price that never moved
1:47 "I will kill you"
2:20 Figuring it out
3:19 The $4.99 chicken
4:05 The real business: the card
5:17 The $130 card
5:47 Why the hot dog matters
6:38 The loop
7:06 Printer ink, inside out
7:29 So how does Costco make money?

Sources
- Costco hot dog (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costco_hot_dog
- Fortune, the Costco CEO hot dog price story (1 Jun 2024): https://fortune.com/2024/06/01/costco-ceo-hot-dog-price-story
- Costco fiscal 2025 results: https://s201.q4cdn.com/287523651/files/doc_news/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025-Operating-Results-2025.pdf
- Costco Form 10-K, fiscal 2025 (SEC): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/909832/000090983225000101/cost-20250831.htm
- Costco's $4.99 rotisserie chicken (Fox Business): https://www.foxbusiness.com/money/costco-rotisserie-chicken-price
- Costco (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costco

"11 cents of every dollar" and "roughly half of operating profit" are our own calculations from Costco's reported fiscal 2025 figures, labelled on screen. The rising bars for rent, gas and cinema tickets are illustrative. Costco is named for commentary only; this channel is not connected to Costco. Education only, not financial or investment advice. Narration voice is AI-generated; script, research and animation made for this channel.
